subject: Savings bridge & architectural Q&A — Optimize toolkit (batching / quant) — FinRise
messages:
From: Olivia Barnes <obarnes@finrise.ai>
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai
Cc: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@finrise.ai>, FinRise Procurement <procurement@finrise.ai>
Date: 2027-07-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick pricing question on Optimize toolkit (batching + quantization)

Hi Irene —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We liked the latency numbers and the KV caching approach. Procurement asked for a short note: we need to understand how Redwood thinks about packaging the Optimize toolkit (credits vs. a flat add-on) and whether you have an approach for upfront pilot discounts tied to batching/caching adoption and quantization work.

Two specific asks:
- Does Redwood recommend a committed credit pool or a per-token add-on for customers that will aggressively use prefix/KV caching?
- For quantization, do you offer an applied engineering credit (e.g., 20–40 hours of SE work) as part of a commercial package, or is that billed separately?

Can you share a short example offer we can show legal/procurement?

Cheers,
Olivia Barnes
Head of AI Platforms, FinRise

From: irene_choi@redwood.ai
To: Olivia Barnes <obarnes@finrise.ai>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-07-25T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick pricing question on Optimize toolkit (batching + quantization)

Hi Olivia — great question. Quick summary below plus an attached example offer tailored for mid-sized fintechs like FinRise. I'll call out three pragmatic packaging patterns we've seen work well.

1) Committed credits + Optimize Add-on (recommended)
   - Structure: Commit to monthly token credits (covers baseline generation/embeddings) + fixed "Optimize toolkit" surcharge (metered by number of seats or models).
   - Why: Credits smooth spend variance; the Optimize surcharge funds tooling (auto-batching suggestions, cache lifecycle) and access to our quantization playbooks. Works when you want predictable cost and operational guarantees.

2) Usage-only + pilot credits
   - Structure: No long-term commit. Redwood provides a pilot credit pool (30–60k tokens) + 1–2 weeks of SE hours as a one-time onboarding credit.
   - Why: Good for proof-of-concept where you plan to evaluate batching & KV cache benefits before committing.

3) Reserved throughput + outcome credits (for strict latency SLAs)
   - Structure: Reserved GPU capacity + monthly optimize credits applied to operational tooling and priority routing.
   - Why: When throughput/latency SLAs matter more than unit cost.

Quantization & SE hours
- We typically include a small engineering credit (8–32 hours) in pilot offers to cover evaluation and a quantization recommendation (model variant + quant profile). Larger applied quantization (quantizing and validating model in prod) is scoped and billed via a fixed services fee or applied credit in the committed contract.

Discounting guidance
- For 12+ month commits we commonly apply a 10–18% effective discount to token pricing, plus a one-time optimization credit worth ~10–20% of the first-quarter billing to fund initial SE work.
- For pilots turning into commits within 90 days, we fold the pilot credits into the first billing cycle and increase committed discounts by 2–4%.

I've attached a sample offer & a simple batching savings model that shows how caching/quantization can change unit economics. Aditya — tagging you for proposed concession bands & seat pricing. Connor — can you add a short note on the expected latency delta when quantizing down to int8 for the B-series models?

Attached: FinRise_Optimize_Toolkit_Offer_v1.pdf, batching_savings_model_finrise.xlsx

Best,
Irene Choi
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai, Olivia Barnes <obarnes@finrise.ai>
Cc: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-07-26T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick pricing question on Optimize toolkit (batching + quantization)

Thanks Irene. Olivia — a few pragmatic guardrails from the AE side so procurement can model economics quickly:

- Pilot ask: Offer 50k pilot tokens + 16 SE hours to scope quantization impact and run a KV-prefix eval on your 1–2 flagship flows. We recommend the pilot run for 4 weeks.
- Commit bands: For a 12-month commit, tier the credit bands: $10k/mo, $25k/mo, $60k/mo — higher tiers unlock 15%–20% off token list price and 25–40 SE hours of onboarding/optimization credits.
- Bundling: Bundle the Optimize toolkit as a per-model seat at $1,200/mo per prod model (waived for the first 2 months in mid-tier band). That seat includes access to the Optimize dashboard and 24/7 routing priority for fallbacks.

Concessions we can give up front (subject to approval):
- One-time signing credit equal to 15% of first quarter invoice (applied as tokens).
- Additional 8–16 SE hours for quantization if customer commits to 12 months within 60 days of pilot close.

If you want, I can convert these bullets into a quick-redline-friendly offer table for procurement.

—Aditya
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Olivia Barnes <obarnes@finrise.ai>
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, connor_obrien@redwood.ai, FinRise Procurement <procurement@finrise.ai>, Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@finrise.ai>
Date: 2027-07-27T10:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick pricing question on Optimize toolkit (batching + quantization)

Thanks — this is helpful. Procurement pushed back on two items:
1) The per-model seat fee — they prefer a credits-only structure and want the Optimize functionality bundled into token economics rather than a separate seat charge.
2) The SE hour framing — procurement would like a clearer AMOUNT of included professional services up front (they asked for a 'zero-surprise' fixed line item).

We are receptive to a 12-month commit but would need: a) an explicit fixed-services line (e.g., 40 hours at a fixed $X or included as a defined credit), and b) an approach to show how caching/quantization will likely change monthly usage so finance can forecast.

Can you produce a one-pager that converts your proposed commit bands into: effective token price after discounts, one-time signing credit amount, included SE hours (fixed), and a simple sensitivity table for monthly tokens when caching/quantization is applied? We'll take that into legal/finance next week.

Also, any constraints around using your quantization recommendations in our private deployment? We need to ensure we can apply the changes within our VPC without extra entanglement.

—Olivia

From: irene_choi@redwood.ai
To: Olivia Barnes <obarnes@finrise.ai>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-07-28T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick pricing question on Optimize toolkit (batching + quantization)

Olivia — thanks for the clarity; we can do everything you asked. Attached is a one-page summary captured from the example offer (PDF) with the commit-band table translated into an explicit model for procurement. High-level answers below: 

1) Seat fee vs credits: we will waive the per-model seat fee if you take a 12-month credit commit at the mid or upper band ($25k/mo or $60k/mo). Optimize features will be bundled into the effective token rate.

2) Fixed services: for the 12-month mid-tier band ($25k/mo) we include 40 SE hours at a fixed $0 line (included); for upper band ($60k/mo) we include 80 SE hours. If you select the pilot -> commit conversion path, we add an extra 16 hours after sign.

3) Forecast sensitivity: see the attached spreadsheet — examples show typical token consumption reductions of 18–35% after KV-prefix caching plus an additional 10–18% improvement from int8 quantization on B-series models (numbers depend on request distribution). We included a conservative and aggressive scenario.

4) Private deployment constraints: our quantization recommendations are implementation-level guidance. For Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) customers we provide the quantization artifacts and test harness; FinRise retains the deployment commits. We do require a short security attestation for any HSM/KMS changes if you want us to run applied validation inside your VPC. This is standard.

Next steps: I will export the one-pager into a procurement-friendly PDF and send a DocuSign-ready MSA + SOW with the fixed-services lines filled. Aditya — please approve the early-signing credit concession (15% first-quarter tokens) and the SE-hour increments so I can include in the DocuSign bundle. Connor — quick note on latency: our expectation for int8 on B-series is ~6–12% faster p50 and ~8–20% faster p95 in common generation workloads; I'll let Connor paste the short latency note in the final doc.

I'll send the finalized PDF + DocuSign links by EOD.

Best,
Irene
